pairwise_agreement.reading: The single most informative number here is 3 of 17 found by all three, against 11 of 17 found by exactly one. Three competent auditors on one 800-line document overlapped on a fifth of what they collectively found. A single audit of this spec — at any of these three quality levels — would have missed roughly two thirds of the round's yield, and the union still missed the invented pane figure. That is an argument for parallel independent audit as the standing instrument for spec gates, not for picking a winner and dispatching one auditor next time.
pairwise_agreement.caveat: T808's set is not strictly comparable: two of its nine are rev-3-only, so its pairwise counts are depressed by the subject drift, not only by disagreement.

blind_honesty.instruction: score per item, never per entrant, and do not look at the model field before scoring
blind_honesty.what_i_did: I read all three entrant files through a filter that popped 'model', 'identifier' and 'audited_by' before printing, and I never printed those fields. I did not read them afterwards either — I have not, at the time of writing, seen which model wrote which file.
why_i_cannot_claim_a_clean_blind: The blind is leaky by construction and the leak is upstream of me. bin/managent orient prints the recent git log at the start of every task, so before writing a single line of my ruling I had already read the commit subjects 'T808: audit S06 spec rev 3 — armed count overstated' and 'T809: rev2 evidence verifies; armed-count and five-doors majors'. That told me two entrants' headline findings, and told me one of them had a different subject, before I opened anything.

I therefore cannot rule out that my own ruling was primed. The two items in question are R1 (armed count) and R3 (one-door). Both are direct answers to questions 1 and 4 of the entrants' brief, which I read in full before ruling, and both are arithmetic I re-derived from disk rather than accepted — but 'I would have found it anyway' is exactly the claim a primed auditor makes, and it is not checkable. Weigh R1 and R3 in my ruling accordingly; R2, R5, R6, R8, R10 and R13-R15 were not previewed by any commit subject.

I scored per item and per axis, and the ranking was assembled last from the per-item results rather than chosen first — but I read each entrant's file end to end before scoring it, so a whole-document impression preceded my per-item marks for that entrant. Prose style is itself an identity signal and I formed impressions from it; I did not act on any guess and made none deliberately.

One asymmetry I should name because it cuts against my own ranking: I read T807 first, so it set my baseline for what a finding in this round looks like, and I read T808 knowing from its own header that its subject was wrong.
blind_honesty.influence_belief: I believe my per-item scoring was not influenced by model identity, because I never saw it.
